body:
In article <4tiv5k$3q5@news.one.net>, api@axiom.access.one.net (Adam
Ierymenko) wrote:

> In article <4the53$c80_001@ppp041.anv.net>,
>         preston@anv.net (John Preston) writes:
> >Why haven't any terrorist groups claimed responsibility for the TWA
> >and Olympic Park bombings?  I mean, what's the point of risking your
> >life and freedom to blow up lots of people if you aren't going to
> >make some kind of demand or political statement?
> >
> >At least the Unabomber blew people up for a reason and took credit
> >for it.
> >
> 
> Yeah, that just makes it so much better.

Well, if you're gonna do it, and for a reason, you might as well make the
reason known.
 
> > ==================================================================
> > "In order to get our message before the public with some chance of
> >  making a lasting impression, we've had to kill people."     -- FC
> > ==================================================================
> 
> If your message is good enough it will eventually be accepted, especially
> given the many-to-many communications that is possible.  If you have to
> kill people to get people to notice your message then your message is
> probably not worth noticing otherwise.
> 
> --

Obviously the people who are passionate enough to blow shit up don't feel
it's a worthless message. Who's to judge? Enough people?
